body: Quick pass (M5) at 678c4832: it merges cleanly, the quick gate is green per the author's run, the body is complete (Fixes #1633, Changelog, Not exercised, and the goldens it shares with #1577 listed), and #1633 is P1, not paused. Flagged ready for M3's safety-tier review.

Review fixes pushed. New head: `ab1509c4eb06a1a93f136b73e65ab2c58d5c9846` (a plain push on top of 678c4832; the PR stays a draft).

1. **The clearance plane over the tool-change X/Y is taken on trust.** The decision file (`docs/decisions/1633-fanuc-first-traverse-clearance.md`, "Taken on trust") and the body's "Not exercised" now say it plainly:
   - The Z-only rapid at the tool-change X/Y trusts the stated clearance plane (else the retract plane) to clear everything under that X/Y: vise, fixture, tool rack, rotary table.
   - The post cannot know what is there.
   - This is safer than main's combined diagonal when the tip stood below the part top. It is **not** safer when something under that X/Y is taller than the clearance.

2. **Two more cases are named as taken on trust, in the same places:**
   - **G43.4 with an unknown rotary pose (fanuc, doosan-dnm).** The Z / X / Y lines come after the arm, with the rotaries at the previous section's pose. No control has run it.
   - **The Doosan index path.** The Z move runs in G43 with the table clamped at its previous index.

3. **A refused first traverse now writes no move, in all six posts.** `xyFirst` returns false on the refusal, and every motion hook returns without writing its move:
   - `onRapid`, `onLinear`, `onCircular`, `onCycle`, `onProbeMove` and `onProbeGuard`, plus the TNC's four hooks.
   - X/Y stay unknown, so every later motion of that section is refused the same way, and the warning still counts once. I chose to refuse the rest of the section rather than skip one move: skipping one would post the next moves from a position no block reached.
   - No combined `G00 X.. Y.. Z..` reaches the program text.
   - `a_first_traverse_with_no_stated_plane_is_refused_by_name` now also asserts, for every post, that no X/Y motion is written after the refusal: neither the bare traverse nor the combined rapid.
   - **Mutation check:** putting the write back after the refusal (`if (!xyFirst(..)) return;` changed to `xyFirst(..);`) turns that test red for each of the six posts.
   - The decision file says that end-to-end blocking on a warning is the callers' job:
     - The app paths refuse to write (`posting.rs:588`, `posting_mounts.rs:248`, `posting_per_op.rs:168`).
     - The `post` CLI (`post.rs:163`) still writes the file and prints the warnings, by design (its recorded `.refusal` cases). That is why the post itself now leaves the move out.
   - One fixture needed a plane: `axis_direction_cli`'s stream. Until now it passed only because the refused rapid was still written.

**Goldens:** none moved in this push.

**Gate:**
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: post suites ok, app suites ok, 0 failed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

`needs-rework` is left as it is.

@NeoTech and M3, please re-review.

Quick pass (M5) at ab1509c4: it merges cleanly, the quick gate is green per the author's comment, and the body is complete. All three of NeoTech's 07:04Z requests are answered in the comment above. Flagged ready for a re-review of 678c4832..ab1509c4. NeoTech's needs-rework stays until a collaborator's review clears this head.

**Delta re-review @ ab1509c4** (since 678c4832), against the maintainer's 3 requested changes: **clean, all three addressed.**

1. **Tool-change X/Y descent taken on trust:** the decision file and the body now have a "Taken on trust" section. The clearance plane is trusted over everything under the tool-change X/Y: vise, fixture, rack and rotary.
2. **G43.4 and Doosan index:** G43.4 with an unknown rotary pose, and the Doosan index with the table clamped, are named there as taken on trust.
3. **Refusal writes no motion:** `xyFirst` now returns false on the refusal, and every caller (rapid, linear, circular, cycle, probe, probe-guard) returns without writing its move. X/Y stay unknown, so nothing more of the section is written, and the warning counts once. This is done in all six posts.
   - **Mutation (re-run here):** restoring the unconditional write in fanuc's `onRapid` turns `a_first_traverse_with_no_stated_plane_is_refused_by_name` **red**. Restored, `first_traverse_clearance_fanuc_family` passes 9/9.
   - `axis_direction_cli.rs` now states `PARAM ClearancePlane 5`. It had passed only because the refused move was still written. `axis_direction_cli` passes 3/3.

No goldens moved. The earlier review (pullrequestreview-5902527203) stands for the rest of the PR.

The maintainer's `needs-rework` is the maintainer's to clear. This collaborator review of the new head answers its requested changes (PV 32).
Back to draft for the merge-time refresh: 31 NC goldens conflict with main (PR 1577) and are regenerated and checked.

Merge-time refresh: merged `origin/main` (`a3a59d1f6`) into the branch as `588627558` (plain push, reviewed head was `ab1509c4e`). The PR stays a draft; labels untouched.

**Conflicts.** Only 31 NC goldens under `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/` conflicted (main's PR 1577 rewrote their contour moves); no code, `.cps` or test source. Each took main's side and was then regenerated with the suites' own switch (`WRITE_GOLDEN=1` on `conformance`, `control_comp`, `wear_comp`, `program_units`). No golden was edited by hand, and the regeneration changed no file other than these 31.

Files: `contour_{control_comp,disc_hole,plate_with_hole,tangential_lead,wear_comp}.nc` in the fanuc default dir, `haas/`, `mazak/`, `sinumerik/` (5 each); `contour_{disc_hole,plate_with_hole,tangential_lead}.nc` in `doosan-dnm/` and `heidenhain/` (3 each); `contour_plate_with_hole.nc` in `inch/{fanuc,haas,mazak,doosan-dnm,sinumerik}/` (5).

**Rule checked by script, file by file, against main's version:** exactly one inserted Z-only rapid immediately before the first X/Y traverse, with the Z of that traverse; no X/Y word before it; every other line identical; in N-numbered files the later block numbers shift by one step (10) with the content after the N-word identical.

| Group | Files | Strict rule |
|---|---|---|
| unnumbered (fanuc 5, haas 5, mazak 5, doosan-dnm 3, inch 4) | 22 | 22 pass |
| sinumerik (5) + inch/sinumerik (1) | 6 | 6 pass |
| heidenhain | 3 | 0 pass |
| total | 31 | 28 pass |

The 3 Heidenhain files differ from the strict rule in two dialect facts, both also in the reviewed head's own Heidenhain goldens, accepted by the coordinating session as within the rule:
1. the program-start words `G40 G90` ride the first motion block, which is now the Z-only rapid, so the traverse after it no longer carries them;
2. the fixed end block `N99999999 %VMC_3-AXIS G71 *` keeps its number.

A relaxed check that allows exactly these two facts and nothing else (same insertion, same Z, all other content identical, +10 on every other block number) passes all 3.

Also checked: 121 goldens differ from main after the merge, exactly the 121 this PR changed at the reviewed head; none outside that set. Of the 90 that did not conflict, 89 are byte-identical to the reviewed head and 1 (`thread_mill_external_m8_multi_form.nc`) is a clean git merge that the regeneration reproduced.

Example, unnumbered (`haas/contour_wear_comp.nc` against main):
```diff
 M8
+G0 Z10
 G0 X11 Y-3 Z10
```
Example, numbered (`sinumerik/contour_wear_comp.nc` against main; 51 insertions, 50 deletions):
```diff
-N50 G0 X11 Y-3 Z10
-N60 G0 X11 Y-3 Z7
-N70 G1 X11 Y-3 Z5 F200
+N50 G0 Z10
+N60 G0 X11 Y-3 Z10
+N70 G0 X11 Y-3 Z7
+N80 G1 X11 Y-3 Z5 F200
```
Example, Heidenhain (`heidenhain/contour_disc_hole.nc` against main):
```diff
-N70 G00 G40 G90 X+42.458 Y-4.861 Z+5*
-N80 G00 X+42.458 Y-4.861 Z+2*
+N70 G00 G40 G90 Z+5*
+N80 G00 X+42.458 Y-4.861 Z+5*
+N90 G00 X+42.458 Y-4.861 Z+2*
 ...
 N99999999 %VMC_3-AXIS G71 *
```

**Delta class:** DELTA (`cargo xtask merge-plan --delta 1636 --reviewed ab1509c4e`): the merge is hand-resolved in these 31 goldens only, so a read-only delta review of `git show --remerge-diff 588627558` is what is owed.

**Tests (Windows, local, on the merged tree):**
- `conformance` 7, `control_comp` 5, `wear_comp` 5, `program_units` 7: all pass without the update switch.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main` fell back to batch (the diff against main touches `crates/cl`): 9 steps, 49 min. Geometry, cl, tools, post, sim, motion and ui suites and `clippy -D warnings` are green. App suites: 407 binaries green, 1 red: `import_step_guard::a_lowered_cap_refuses_the_same_face_at_once`, "import did not finish within 30s", the known flake of issue 1605 (noted, not touched).
- Not exercised: release-tier heavy lanes, pixel snapshots, other operating systems.
